newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Daily wheat export tax set to be adopted.
newsitem.headline: Daily wheat export tax set to be adopted.

text.p: The European Commission is expected on Wednesday to override French opposition and approve a tax on daily exports of wheat grain and flour, Commission sources said.
The proposed tax of 15 ecus a tonne on soft wheat grain and 20 ecus a tonne on wheat flour exports was suspended last week after French EU Commissioner Edith Cresson objected.
"Yes, I think it will now go through," said one source, speaking after the issue had been discussed by the EU commissioners' aides.

Previously unanimity was required because the proposal had been submitted under the so-called written procedure. Now it only requires a simple majority at the weekly commissioners' meeting in Strasbourg.
Cresson argued that the tax, which is aimed at saving scarce supplies for domestic consumers, was no longer needed because wheat prices were now falling.
But sources said that the fall was partly due to expectations of the tax.

Trade sources added that the week's delay meant had enabled nearly all exporters with special "nil-value" export licences to customs clear their grain and would therefore not be liable to pay the tax.
